title: Adjustment Cause
description: Structured account of why a post-order adjustment occurred. Adjustment `type` records what was done about it (a refund, a credit, a dispute); this records what went wrong. The three axes are independent and MUST NOT be collapsed: `category` is what failed, `attributed_to` is which party the recording system holds responsible, and `nature` is whether it appears deliberate. A mistake by a business and abuse by a business share a category and differ in nature; an incorrect amount can originate with any party. All fields are optional, and a recording system SHOULD omit any axis it cannot determine rather than guessing. Values are assertions by the system recording them, not adjudications: the same event may be recorded differently by a platform and a business, and nothing here establishes liability.

category.description: What went wrong. Open string; the values below are the well-known set and implementations MAY use others. Most are not specific to agent-originated transactions and apply equally where a person transacted directly.

category_description.description: Human-readable account of the cause, for categories the well-known set does not capture.

attributed_to.description: The role the recording system considers responsible. Open string; the values below are the well-known set. `none` records that the cause was established and no party is held responsible, which is distinct from omitting the field because responsibility is unknown.

nature.description: Whether the cause appears deliberate, and if so of what kind. `error` is an honest mistake by a party acting in good faith. `fault` is a technical failure with no intent. `abuse` is deliberate exploitation of the rules as written by a party that asserted nothing false: it is who it claims to be and its statements were true. `fraud` is a false assertion — of identity, entitlement, or a material fact — made to obtain what would not otherwise be given. The distinction between the two is whether a false assertion was made, and it is not merely descriptive: fraud carries reporting obligations under payment scheme rules and applicable law that abuse does not, so a party that cannot make the determination MUST record `undetermined` rather than choose. `compromise` is a party whose behavior was directed by someone else, including through manipulated content; the compromised party asserted nothing false and is not the deceiver. `disagreement` is a case where no party malfunctioned and the parties read the same transaction differently. `undetermined` records that the question was considered and not resolved.

layer.description: Where in the transaction the cause arose. `intent` is what the principal wanted; `authority` is what the acting party was permitted to do; `identity` is who a party was; `interaction` is the exchange between the parties, including anything a counterparty supplied that influenced it; `payment` is the movement of money; `fulfillment` is the delivery of what was purchased. A cause can be recorded at the layer it arose in even when it surfaced later.

scope.description: The level at which the cause is expressed. A single transaction can be unremarkable on its own and anomalous as part of a task, a pattern by one actor, or a period. Recording the level distinguishes an adjustment for one bad transaction from one covering a run of them.

level.description: `transaction` is this order alone. `task` is a set of transactions carried out toward one objective, which may span businesses. `actor` is a pattern in one party's behavior across tasks. `counterparty` is a pattern in dealings with one other party. `period` is an aggregate over time, such as a spending window.

reference.description: Identifier for the scope instance, where one exists: a task identifier, an actor identifier, or a period label. Resolvable by the recording system; opaque to others.

affected_count.description: Number of transactions the cause is understood to affect, where known. Present when the adjustment addresses one of several.

authority_reference.description: Reference to the grant of authority the transaction was carried out under, where the cause concerns authority or intent. Resolvable by the party that issued it.

evidence_uri.description: Location of the record supporting this cause — a transaction log, an execution record, a signed attestation. Access is governed by the publishing party; the field records that evidence exists and where to ask for it.

determined_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the cause was determined, which may be substantially later than the adjustment's `occurred_at`.

determined_by.description: The role that made this determination, using the same well-known values as `attributed_to`. A cause recorded by the party it attributes responsibility to carries different weight than one recorded by a counterparty, and a reader cannot tell the two apart without this field.
